text: Debugging is an essential skill for any programmer. When a program does not work as expected, the first step is identifying bugs by observing the symptoms and finding where the problem occurs. Good debugging tools, such as breakpoints and step-by-step execution, help you examine what the code is actually doing. However, tools alone are not enough. You should follow a systematic approach: form a hypothesis, test it, and narrow down the cause instead of changing code randomly. Logging is also very useful, because well-placed log messages show what happened before an error. By combining careful observation, the right tools, a logical method, and clear logs, you can solve problems faster and with less frustration.
